project: Shadow (Rust MoE inference engine, repo J:\Shadow on this PC)
task: Two-part plan agreed with the human: (1) hybrid read path - the one 'untried' line in the notes; (2) then the Avalon port per docs/EXPERIMENT_SPEC_2026-11-01.json.
the_physics: The copy engine can only DMA from pinned memory - a hardware rule, not a choice. The fast path (OS file cache, ~50 GiB of the 89 GiB model, memory speed) is pageable, so its bytes must be copied into pinned staging first: bytes cross DRAM three times (page cache -> pinned read+write, pinned -> link). DRAM is ~30 GB/s total; the copy engine measures 13, the link ceiling is 23-28. Two copy streams measured a TIE (65.0 vs 65.5 s) - scheduling is not the problem, traffic is. The GPU waiting on the copy is now ~677 ms a pass, roughly a fifth of a prompt pass - the copy is the critical path.

task_1_hybrid_read_path.what_to_build: A hybrid policy: bytes the file cache already holds (the ~50 GiB hot set) keep the current buffered path; genuinely cold bytes go direct-I/O (unbuffered) straight into the pinned buffer, overlapped into an event pool - the notes' exact 'Untried: overlapped reads into an event pool' line. Gate behind SHADOW_DIRECT_IO=1; baseline stays default until measured.
task_1_hybrid_read_path.why_it_might_win: Skips one DRAM trip for cold bytes: two touches instead of three.
task_1_hybrid_read_path.why_it_might_lose: Direct I/O loses the file cache, and unbuffered reads always go to the NVMe at its 3.5 GB/s ceiling. For hot bytes the triple path at memory speed beats it; only cold bytes can win, and the tier amortizes most of the rest.
task_1_hybrid_read_path.honest_odds: ~50/50, expected gain 10-25% on prompt-heavy, ~0 on decode (decode already has the tier warm)

task_2_avalon: Run second, per the old spec's own logic: if task 1 wins, Avalon's payoff multiplies. Its spec is docs/EXPERIMENT_SPEC_2026-11-01.json - do not rewrite it, just execute it. ~40% odds, ceiling ~1.4x, kernel already fast enough at 17-21 GB/s on 14 threads, AVX-512 present (family 6 model 167, verified via CPUID - the notes' premises were wrong once on this).

the_honest_ceiling: Neither task alone is 2x. Task 1 + task 2 + the IQ2_S quant bench (kernels already built and tested, quality band is the risk) is the honest path to 1.5-2x; all three fight over the same DRAM bus, so the landing zone is not a clean 2x.
